Let \(m=n/2=2q^2\). I claim the required number is

\[
\boxed{\ell^{r-3}(\ell^{r-1}-1)\bigl((\ell-1)^r-(-1)^r\bigr)}.
\]

Here is the derivation.

For \(\sigma\in\Gamma\) with \(\pi_\sigma=\pi\), write

\[
\sigma(\alpha_i^{(j)})=\zeta^{a_i^{(j)}}\alpha_{\pi(i)}^{(j)},\qquad
\sigma(\rho_j)=\zeta^{s_j}\rho_j .
\]

The product relations give

\[
\sum_i a_i^{(j)}=0\quad (j<r),\qquad
\sum_i a_i^{(r)}=\sum_j s_j .
\]

Since \(\pi\) is a product of \(m=2q^2\) transpositions, let \(X\) run over the transposition-pairs and define

\[
A_X=(a_i^{(1)}+a_{\pi(i)}^{(1)},\dots,a_i^{(r)}+a_{\pi(i)}^{(r)})\in\mathbb F_\ell^r .
\]

Conjugation by the Kummer kernel changes only the antisymmetric parts \(a_i^{(j)}-a_{\pi(i)}^{(j)}\), while conjugation by \(C_{S_n}(\pi)\) permutes the \(m\) pairs. Thus a \(\widetilde C_\pi\)-orbit is determined by

\[
s=(s_1,\dots,s_r)\in(\mathbb F_\ell^\times)^r
\]

and the multiset \(\{A_X\}_{X=1}^m\), with total sum

\[
\sum_X A_X=\Bigl(0,\dots,0,\sum_j s_j\Bigr).
\]

For \(k\in\mathbb F_\ell^r\), the action on \(\Omega_k\) sends

\[
(i,h,u)\mapsto
\bigl(\pi(i),\pi(h),u+k\cdot s+a_i-a_h\bigr).
\]

Squaring gives translation by

\[
2k\cdot s+A_X-A_Y .
\]

Hence a base two-orbit contributes \(\ell^r\) actual \(2\)-cycles exactly when this vector is \(0\). If \(x_v\) is the multiplicity of \(v\in\mathbb F_\ell^r\) among the \(A_X\), and

\[
R(t)=\sum_v x_vx_{v-t},
\]

then the \(2\)-cycle count has the form

\[
C(k)=\ell^r B(t),\qquad t=-2(k_1s_1,\dots,k_rs_r),
\]

where

\[
B(t)=2R(t)-m\mathbf 1_{t=0}.
\]

The required differences force

\[
B=B_O+8\ell(q+3Q)\mathbf 1_U+8\ell^2(q+Q)\mathbf 1_W
\]

for a unique flag \(W\subset U\subset\mathbb F_\ell^r\), \(\operatorname{codim}U=1\), \(\operatorname{codim}W=2\). Fourier transforming gives magnitudes

\[
|\widehat x(\chi)|=
\begin{cases}
2q^2,&\chi=1,\\
q+4Q,&\chi\in U^\perp\setminus\{1\},\\
q+2Q,&\chi\in W^\perp\setminus U^\perp,\\
q,&\chi\notin W^\perp .
\end{cases}
\]

Because \(2\) generates \(\mathbb F_\ell^\times\) and the primes \(q,q+2Q,q+4Q\) are all congruent to \(q\pmod \ell\), they are inert in \(\mathbb Q(\zeta)\). Thus each nonzero Fourier coefficient is forced, up to a common translation, by the displayed magnitude layer. The total-sum condition then fixes that translation uniquely because

\[
m=2q^2\not\equiv0\pmod\ell .
\]

So for each admissible flag and each admissible \(s\), there is exactly one conjugacy orbit.

It remains only to count admissible \(s\) and flags.

First,

\[
s_j\ne0\ \forall j,\qquad S:=\sum_j s_j\ne0,
\]

because \((\sum_j s_j)e_r\in U\setminus W\). The number of \(s\in(\mathbb F_\ell^\times)^r\) with nonzero sum is

\[
(\ell-1)^r-\frac{(\ell-1)^r+(\ell-1)(-1)^r}{\ell}
=
\frac{(\ell-1)\bigl((\ell-1)^r-(-1)^r\bigr)}{\ell}.
\]

Next, the condition \((\sum_j s_j)e_r\in U\setminus W\) is equivalent to

\[
e_r\in U\setminus W.
\]

The number of hyperplanes \(U\subset\mathbb F_\ell^r\) containing \(e_r\) is

\[
\frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}.
\]

For each such \(U\), the number of codimension-one subspaces \(W\subset U\) not containing \(e_r\) is \(\ell^{r-2}\). Hence the number of admissible flags is

\[
\ell^{r-2}\frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}.
\]

Multiplying,

\[
\frac{(\ell-1)\bigl((\ell-1)^r-(-1)^r\bigr)}{\ell}
\cdot
\ell^{r-2}\frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}
=
\ell^{r-3}(\ell^{r-1}-1)\bigl((\ell-1)^r-(-1)^r\bigr).
\]

Therefore the number of required \(\widetilde C_\pi\)-conjugacy orbits is

\[
\boxed{\ell^{r-3}(\ell^{r-1}-1)\bigl((\ell-1)^r-(-1)^r\bigr)}.
\]
